newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says EU members need great effort for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says EU members need great effort for EMU.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Friday Germany and other European Union members must make great efforts to meet the entrance requirements for a single European currency.

The successful completion of European economic and monetary union is an important step in European unity, Kohl said, according to a summary of remarks prepared for delivery at a small business conference. "We want a hard common currency," Kohl said.
The criteria for ensuring stability are not open to renegotiation and must be met, and the same goes for the EMU timetable, Kohl said.

Kohl said he was aware that great efforts were still needed in member states, including Germany, to meet the stability criteria. This shows that reforms must be implemented without hesitation, he said.
A summary of Kohl's remarks was provided by his party, the Christian Democrats.

Rising unemployment and a sluggish economy were increasing fears Germany would fail to keep budget deficits under the EMU limit of 3.0 percent of gross domestic product. Bonn forecast deficits of 2.9 percent of GDP in 1997, the year that determines which countries qualify for the EMU start in 1999. -- Bonn Newsroom, +49-228 26097150
